To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
local rapamycin delivery is effective for the treatment of vein graft disease in short-term vein grafts, but is not effective for long-term treatment of vein grafts.
periadventitial rapamycin-eluted microbeads are associated with local toxicity and poor long term efficacy in experimental vein grafts.
periadventitial rapamycin-eluding microbeads promote vein graft disease in the long-term pig vein-to-carotids interposition model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel, nonthrombogenic and antithrombogenic materials, and the development of new methods to improve the performance of existing materials.
the development of new methods to prevent restenosis in vein grafts.
the development of a new class of drugs for the prevention of vein graft disease and the development of novel drug delivery systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the application of rapamycine-eluting beads to vein grafts has the potential to inhibit vein graft disease in short-term grafts but is not effective in the long term.
the use of local rapamycin delivery to prevent vein graft disease is limited by local toxicity.
the local application of a sustained rapamycin formulation is not effective in the treatment of vein graft disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the application of rapamycine-eluting microbeads to the outside surface of a vein graft in a pig model of vein-to-artery interposition grafts is associated with a short-term reduction in vein graft disease and a paradoxical long-term acceleration in vein graft disease.
local rapamycin application to vein grafts is not an efficacious therapy.
local application of sustained release rapamycin to the vein graft wall does not prevent vein graft disease in the long-term.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rapamycin-elution from polyvinyl alcohol beads is not an effective treatment for vein graft disease.
local toxicity is a major problem in the application of rapamycins in the vascular field, and it is a problem that is not well recognized.
the use of rapamycin in vein graft disease may not be as simple as it appears.
